1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 22.10.2011 PASSED IN MVC NO.1822/2007 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MACT, PUTTUR, SITTING ITINERATE AT BELTHANGADY, D.K., PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.1822/2007 dated 22.10.2011.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.8,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident.

2. The Court below considering the evidence on record had held that the accident had taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle and the Insurance Company had not filed NC: 2023:KHC:37435 the appeal against them.
The only issue that falls consideration before this Court is whether the claimant is entitled for the enhancement of the compensation.
As per Ex.P5 - wound certificate
, the claimant took treatment as inpatient from 27.12.2006 to 29.12.2006 for two days.
As per the wound certificate he had sustained fracture of maxilla, fracture of lower zygomatic complex and one more swelling injury on his mouth.
Ex.P7 is the wound certificate issued by Indira Hospital disclosing that the claimant also took treatment at Indira Hospital as inpatient up to 06.01.2007 for the same injuries.
Considering Exs.P1 to P51, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.20,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
Towards medical expenses incurred by him the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.35,000/-.
3. It is the case of the claimant that he requires future medical expenses.
As there is no evidence on record, the court below had not granted any amount under NC: 2023:KHC:37435 the said head.

Under the head of conveyance, food and nutrition and attendant charges an amount of Rs.3,000/-,
Rs.3,000/- and Rs.2,000/- respectively was granted.
Towards loss of amenities an amount of Rs.5,000/- was granted.
Altogether, compensation of an amount of Rs.68,000/- was granted by the Court below.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Court below has not awarded reasonable compensation.
It is submitted that for the kind of fractures he had suffered, granting an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering is on the lower side.
He submits that he requires future medical expenses and no amount was granted by the Tribunal under that head.

Towards conveyance, nutrition and attendant charges, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.8,000/-
which is on the lower side and no amounts were granted towards transportation.
He submits that granting an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards loss of amenities is on the lower side.

sentences.text: It is submitted that for the fracture he has sustained he could not resume work.
That aspect was not considered and no amounts were granted for the loss of income during the laid up period.
It is submitted that the compensation that was awarded was not reasonable.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that except filing the documents and medical records, he has not examined anyone.
In spite of that, the Court below has granted the compensation.
He submits that no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.

6. In this case the claimant had sustained fracture of maxilla, fracture of lower zygomatic complex and one more swelling injury on his mouth, this fracture to the mouth causes lot of pain and suffering, as he was not in a NC: 2023:KHC:37435 position to resume work for a long time.

Considering these injuries, this Court deems it appropriate to grant an amount of Rs.40,000/-
under the head of pain and suffering.
Towards medical expenses the Court below had rightly granted an amount of Rs.35,000/- and no interference is called for.
Then coming to the future medical expenses without their being any evidence the Tribunal rightly rejected the said request made by the claimant.
Towards attendant charges, transport and nourishment this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.10,000/-.
The amount of Rs.5,000/- granted by the Court below is on the lower side.
For the fractures he had sustained it would definitely take some time for the claimant to resume his work.
The accident had occurred in the year 2007.
This Court is considering the income at Rs.3,500/- for three months = Rs.10,500/- (3,500/- x 3= 10,500/-).
In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA -vs- M.MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
All together the claimant entitled is for amount of Rs.1,10,500/-.

8. The claimant is therefore, entitled to the compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Compensation  Awarded
1. Pain and Agony : Rs. 40,000.00 2.

Medical Expenses : Rs. 35,000.00  Attendant charges, Transport, : Rs. 10,000.00 3.
 Nourishment 4.
Loss of amenities : Rs. 5,000.00  Loss of income during the laid up 5. : Rs. 10,500.00  period 6.
Legal Expenses : Rs. 10,000.00  Total : Rs. Rs.1,10,500/-
